controls.requirement: Every shipped schema is a valid Draft 2020-12 document with a closed root and a schema-identity const.

Every positive instance validates against the schema that judges it. Eight instances, and they are not all the same kind: seven are in-schema examples arrays, one is an external positive instance, because source-disposition.schema.json carries no examples array and instead points x-positive-instance at references/source-disposition/refused-claims.json in the tree.
controls.where: scratch validator, 7 in-schema examples + 1 external positive instance = 8 positive cases

controls.requirement: Every recorded refusal control is actually refused. Thirty-two, and they are not all the same kind: twenty-five are x-refusal-controls carried inside the eight schemas, and seven are the negative_control instances on the seven dispositions in refused-claims.json, each replayed against the schema its schema_id names.
controls.where: scratch validator, 25 in-schema controls + 7 disposition controls = 32 negative probes

controls.requirement: Each control's named keyword is the keyword that actually refuses it. For every one of the thirty-two controls the validator removes exactly the keyword named in refused_by, changes nothing else, and requires the instance to validate afterwards. A control that stays refused after its named guard is gone is refused by something else and proves nothing about the guard it names.
controls.where: scratch validator knockout pass, 32 knockouts, 32 discriminating, 0 surviving
controls.prior_state: FAIL_ON_TWO. DTCR-XC-SD-001 and DTCR-XC-SD-002 carried dispositions arrays of length 1 and 0, so both were refused by properties.dispositions.minItems before reaching $defs.disposition.required and properties.source_ref.required respectively. Both instances have been rebuilt with a complete seven-item dispositions array valid in every other respect and now discriminate on their named keyword. DTCR-XC-SD-001's refused_by additionally names $defs.disposition.allOf[0].then.required, because a REFUSED disposition missing its negative_control is refused by both keywords and naming only one would claim a discrimination the instance cannot show.
controls.supersedes: An earlier revision of this receipt recorded C4 as 'removing any one of the seven refusal guards turns the validator red, so no guard is decorative', evidenced by 'mutation harness, 8 planted defects, 8 killed'. That claim is withdrawn on three counts: the guard count and the defect count did not match each other, the eight defects were never recorded individually so the claim was not replayable, and the harness that produced them was uncommitted and is gone. The per-control knockout recorded above is what was actually run against these bytes and it covers all thirty-two controls rather than eight.

controls.requirement: The seven source dispositions are present, all REFUSED, each with a replayable negative control naming both the schema that refuses it and the keyword inside that schema doing the refusing.
controls.where: scratch validator disposition pass, 7 of 7 REFUSED, 7 of 7 replayed and refused, 7 of 7 discriminating under knockout

controls.requirement: No claim in the shipped prose asserts a refusal broader than the keyword behind it enforces.
controls.where: Shadow BLOCK_C0 findings C-1 and the same-class prose sweep
controls.detail: The plane contract claimed the public schemas have no free-text field wide enough to hold a private locator. That is false and was re-derived here: thirty-six string fields across the eight schemas carry no pattern, enum, const or length ceiling, and two probes confirmed it -- a cloud-drive URL placed in candidate-record replacement_path.note validates, and a file:// URI placed in source-packet disposition_ref validates. The contract now states that identity fields are pattern-closed, that free-text fields are not shape-protected, and that a leak scan over every reachable object is a standing obligation rather than a courtesy. Three same-class overclaims were downgraded with them: the receipt summary refuses ten listed spellings and not a class, the candidate-record target list refuses four anchored case-sensitive spellings and not a class, and the remediation not-clause is a blacklist of three pairs out of fifty-four and not a check on the pairing. SKILL.md and AGENTS.md were swept for the same class and carry none of it.

leak_scan.scan_law: Anything matching the scan and not on the permitted list above is a leak until someone shows otherwise. The list is deliberately short and explicit so a future scan can distinguish a deliberate probe from a real value without asking the author.
leak_scan.self_scope_note: The scan recorded here covers the contract commit this receipt binds as its subject. The receipt commit that carries this file is scanned by the same command in the reporting step, since a receipt cannot scan the commit that carries it any more than it can name its own hash.

evidence_ceiling: DTCR_C0_CONTRACT_REPAIRED_AFTER_SHADOW_BLOCK, READY FOR RE-REVIEW. What is established on these exact bytes: eight closed Draft 2020-12 schemas exist; eight positive instances validate against the schema that judges each, seven of them in-schema examples and one an external file; all thirty-two recorded refusal controls were replayed and refused, twenty-five carried inside the schemas and seven carried by the dispositions; and for every one of the thirty-two, removing exactly the keyword its refused_by names -- and nothing else -- makes the instance validate, so each control discriminates on the guard it names. All seven source dispositions are REFUSED with such a control. What is established about the guards themselves, and is weaker than it previously read: four of the seven headline refusals are structural, and three rest partly on a finite list of spellings or pairs that a paraphrase passes, which is now stated wherever those refusals are described. What is not established: that the schemas contain a private locator by shape -- thirty-six free-text fields accept one, and two probes confirmed it, so the plane split is a rule people follow backed by a leak scan, not a shape that enforces itself; that any adapter exists; that the method has been pointed at a codebase; that a refactor was applied or verified; that a cross-repository migration works; that a consumer can bootstrap from this; or that model quality, runtime portability, production safety, legal clearance, merge or release follow. Every check above came from an uncommitted scratch harness; a committed, CI-routed harness is ABSENT. A contract that survives its own refusal controls has survived its own refusal controls.
